result.title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
result.comment: Published at fifth conference on lifelong learning agents
result.summary: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to adapt to new data (plasticity) while retaining the knowledge acquired from old data (stability). Existing methods are explicitly designed to focus on balancing stability and plasticity to mitigate the challenge of catastrophic forgetting while promoting learning. However, the impact of order and nature of samples from the new data that the network is trained on remains an under explored factor. We argue that a CL algorithm should have the ability to rank incoming samples in terms of their relationship with prior data and their effect on the learning process. In this work, we investigate if scoring and prioritizing incoming data based on their semantic relationships with the model's current knowledge can benefit CL. We propose SACK, short for Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge, a plug and play technique for continual learning methods. SACK dissects categorical knowledge of the model into fine-grained concepts, computes the relationships between previously learned concepts and new concepts in each experience, and uses this relationship knowledge for prioritizing new samples. Experiments across several types of CL methods (regularization, replay, and prompt based) in class incremental and task incremental settings demonstrate that integration of SACK not only improves accuracy and reduces forgetting but also handles long tail distribution, helps focus on semantically interpretable regions, and yields better calibrated and robust models compared to prior approaches.

AI.brief_summary: 提出即插即用的 SACK：将模型的类别知识拆解为细粒度概念，计算已学概念与新经验中概念的关系，并据此对新样本排序，配合正则化、回放与 prompt 类持续学习方法提升准确率、减少遗忘。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无直接关系，但「按与当前知识的语义关系给样本打分排序」这一训练侧机制可能可供核查，用于 latent 推理轨迹或视觉证据样本的优先级筛选与监督分配；其本身不涉及多模态推理状态或 latent 生成，迁移需较多论证。
